terms.definition: A cell with its genetic material enclosed in a nucleus, such as a plant or animal cell.
terms.examiner: Plant, animal and fungal cells are all eukaryotic.

terms.definition: A much smaller cell with no nucleus: its genetic material is a single DNA loop in the cytoplasm, and it may also have plasmids.
terms.examiner: Bacteria are prokaryotes. They have a cell wall, but it is not made of cellulose.

terms.definition: A small ring of DNA found in bacterial cells, separate from the main DNA loop.
terms.examiner: Plasmids are used as vectors in genetic engineering.

terms.definition: Where most of the reactions of aerobic respiration take place, releasing energy for the cell.

terms.examiner: Found in prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

terms.definition: Where photosynthesis takes place; contains chlorophyll, which absorbs light.
terms.examiner: Root hair cells have no chloroplasts: there is no light underground.

terms.definition: Made of cellulose in plants and algae; strengthens the cell and supports it.
terms.examiner: Do not confuse with the cell membrane, which controls what enters and leaves.

terms.definition: How many times bigger the image is than the real object: magnification = size of image ÷ size of real object.
terms.examiner: Convert both sizes to the same unit first. 1 mm = 1000 µm.

terms.definition: The ability to distinguish between two points that are close together.
terms.examiner: Electron microscopes have a higher resolution as well as a higher magnification, so they show sub-cellular structures such as ribosomes.

terms.definition: Steps to stop unwanted microorganisms contaminating a culture, such as sterilising the loop in a flame and lifting the lid only slightly.
terms.examiner: Plates are incubated at 25 °C in schools so that human pathogens do not grow.
